items.description: Find the tells in your tale. TellTale reads fiction at two levels, the sentences and the story underneath them, and catches what line edits miss: stakes that never rise, a theme the narrator spells out. It ranks what to fix first, for one chapter or a whole manuscript in Markdown, Word, EPUB, or PDF. A craft signal, not an AI detector.

skills.name: 52dc26c1-49d3-48c6-b4c8-75d17e55bd7d:telltale

The line-level layer covers sentence craft such as stock phrasing, not-X-but-Y reversals, forced triads, em-dash habits, and one-line closers. The structural layer, based on the StoryScope study of AI fiction, covers flat event escalation, over-explained themes, tidy single-track plots, too-clean agency, moral certainty, and strictly linear time. Modes are assess (default, no edits), score (per-dimension scores plus an overall reader-notice rating), and revise (suggested rewrites that never silently change plot or meaning). Use when a writer asks whether their story reads as AI-written, wants AI tells found or fixed in fiction, or wants narrative-structure critique of an AI-assisted draft. Gives a writing-quality signal, not an authorship verdict. Not for essays, marketing copy, or other non-fiction.

commands.description: Score fiction 0-5 on 10 structural and 7 line-level dimensions, with an overall reader-notice rating.

commands.description: Suggest rewrites that remove AI tells from fiction without changing plot or meaning.

items.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69

items.author: 3Flux

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcangel
skills.description: Surface the 10 strongest signals that would make a champion VC go to bat for your startup. Usage: /vcangel. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and produces an enthusiastic champion's brief: each signal, why it wins the room, and how to amplify it. Saves to vcangel.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcdebrief
skills.description: Debrief a VC meeting and produce a follow-up email, open diligence queue, and next-step recommendation. Usage: /vcdebrief vcmatch-report.md. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and the vcmatch report. Saves to vcdebrief-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcdevil
skills.description: Stress-test your startup with the 10 hardest VC questions. Usage: /vcdevil. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and produces a brutal adversarial interrogation: each question, why it's lethal, and a rebuttal framework. Saves to vcdevil.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcintro
skills.description: Draft VC outreach from a vcmatch report. Usage: /vcintro vcmatch-report.md. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and the vcmatch report, then produces three outreach variants: cold email, warm intro request, and LinkedIn DM. Saves to vcintro-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vclist
skills.description: Build a prioritized VC target list from the active startup profile. Usage: /vclist. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md, researches the VC landscape, and produces a tiered list of 15–20 funds ranked by fit with rationale and suggested contact angle. Saves to vclist.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vclp
skills.description: Generate a fund-specific one-page executive summary from a vcmatch report. Usage: /vclp vcmatch-report.md. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and the vcmatch report, then produces a one-pager written entirely in the fund's language and framed around their thesis. Saves to vclp-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcmatch
skills.description: Match the active startup profile against a VC fund. Usage: /vcmatch VC Fund Name [profile-file.md]. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md by default (or the profile file if provided), spawns 4 parallel domain research sub-agents, and produces a structured VC Match Report with 8-dimension fit scoring summing to /100, portfolio pattern analysis, deal process intel, and warm intro paths.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcpartner
skills.description: Deep profile on a specific VC partner. Usage: /vcpartner fund partner name. Researches the partner's background, personal thesis, portfolio companies they've led, public writing, and speaking topics. Produces conversation starters and a fit assessment against the active startup profile. Saves to vcpartner-fund-lastname.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcperks
skills.description: Research the full value a VC fund delivers beyond the check — credits, services, brand signal, strategic expertise, media amplification, policy access, and follow-on capital pathway — scored by relevance to the active startup. Usage: /vcperks VC Fund Name. Saves to vcperks-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcposer
skills.description: Detect VC funds that are posers: zombie funds, stage drifters, thesis cosplayers, and tourist investors who take meetings but don't write checks. Usage: /vcposer VC Fund Name. Runs 8 evidence-based checks, scores a Poser Score (0–100), and recommends whether to pursue. Saves to vcposer-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcprep
skills.description: Prepare a 15-minute VC pitch meeting from the active startup profile and a vcmatch report. Usage: /vcprep vcmatch-report.md. Produces a complete meeting prep: timed agenda, opening hook, slide-by-slide talking points, preemptive answers to the fund's likely diligence questions, red flag rebuttals, and a clear ask.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcraise
skills.description: Generate a fundraising strategy memo from the active startup profile and any existing vcmatch/vclist files. Usage: /vcraise. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md and any vcmatch-*.md or vclist.md files in the current directory, then produces a full fundraising strategy: sequencing, milestones, timeline, and this week's next actions. Saves to vcraise.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vcterm
skills.description: Analyze a VC term sheet against market norms, flag founder-unfriendly clauses, score founder-friendliness, and produce a ranked negotiation priority list. Usage: /vcterm termsheet-file.md. Reads STARTUP_PROFILE.md. Saves to vcterm-fund.md.

skills.name: c337397e-994f-4f3c-a160-7febf0e31e69:vctrack
skills.description: Scan all vc*.md output files and generate a pipeline status dashboard. Usage: /vctrack. Reads vcmatch/vcposer/vcintro/vcprep/vcdebrief files in the current directory. Saves to vctrack.md.

Use quando alguém pedir "faz o fluxo completo", "abre o PR", "qual o processo pra entregar isso", "como organizar branch e PR", "/fluxo-dev", ou quando uma tarefa de código precisa chegar até produção.

items.description: GDPR operations for controllers, law firms and DPOs, in four skills. gdpr-breach-72h-en runs a personal data breach through Art. 33-34: is it a breach, the risk factors from EDPB Guidelines 9/2022, notification to the supervisory authority without undue delay with the 72-hour outer limit counted from awareness, communication to individuals and its exemptions, and the internal breach register. gdpr-dpia-en decides whether a DPIA is required (Art. 35(3) cases, the national lists, the nine WP248

skills.name: 22cc1dd1-6cf1-4c5f-af67-f99b84852282:gdpr-breach-72h-en
skills.description: Personal data breach response assistant grounded in GDPR Art. 33-34, EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 on breach notification, and national supervisory-authority breach forms. Runs the decision tree: (1) is it a breach and which type (confidentiality/integrity/availability), (2) risk assessment to rights and freedoms, (3) notify the SA without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72h (Art. 33) - with a counter for the 72h outer limit from awareness, (4) communicate to data subjects (Art. 34, "high risk") + exemptions, (5) internal breach register entry (Art. 33(5)). Drafts the notification and communications - it does NOT send to the SA or to data subjects (human acts). Adds no connectors and makes no outbound calls of its own; the incident details you paste still go to the model you have configured. Use when: "data leak", "GDPR breach", "72-hour notification", "do we notify individuals", "Art. 33", "breach response".

skills.description: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) assistant grounded in GDPR Art. 35-36, the Article 29 Working Party guidelines WP248 rev.01, and national supervisory-authority lists. Walks through: (1) the threshold test - is a DPIA REQUIRED (WP248's 9 criteria, the ">=2" rule of thumb, Art. 35(3) mandatory cases, the SA's mandatory list), (2) the DPIA structure mandated by Art. 35(7) (systematic description, necessity & proportionality, risk assessment, mitigating measures), (3) the Art. 36 prior-consultation decision. Drafts the DPIA and a decision log - it does NOT make the controller's risk decision or file with the authority (those are human acts). Adds no connectors and makes no outbound calls of its own; the system description you paste still goes to the model you have configured. Use when: "do I need a DPIA", "data protection impact assessment", "DPIA for profiling/CCTV/AI", "Art. 35 GDPR", "prior consultation", "high-risk processing".

Identifies the request type (access 15, rectification 16, erasure 17, restriction 18, portability 20, objection 21, automated decisions 22), tracks the DEADLINE (one month from receipt at the latest, Art. 12(3); +2 months where complexity or number of requests require it), gates exemptions and refusal grounds (e.g. Art. 17(3), manifestly unfounded/excessive requests - Art. 12(5)), and drafts the response + a request register. Identity verification of the requester (Art. 12(6)) comes first. It does NOT send responses or erase data (human acts). The skill itself adds no connectors and makes no outbound calls; the text you put in front of it still reaches whatever model you have configured, so keep the request file out of the prompt or point the agent at a local model. Use when: "subject access request", "erasure request", "right to be forgotten", "objection", "DSAR deadline", "data portability".

items.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871
items.description: A 7-step discovery pipeline for product managers: reconcile messy interview transcripts, extract evidence per persona, find where personas collide, frame the problem, scope v1 with a cut list, pick the riskiest assumption, then build and critique a prototype. skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:discovery-to-mvp

skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:interview-guide

skills.description: Scopes a v1 from a framed problem and discovery evidence — what v1 does, what it explicitly doesn't, a cut list where every cut has a reason, a cost and a revisit trigger, and an adoption plan for getting busy users off their current channel. skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:persona-collide

skills.description: Pulls one persona's evidence out of a merged interview transcript — pains with verbatim quotes and severity, workarounds, numbers, prompted vs unprompted signals, stated vs revealed gaps, what must not change, and conspicuous silences — every line tied to a turn ID. skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:problem-framing
skills.description: Turns discovery evidence into a solution-free problem statement under 80 words, compares it with how the original brief framed the problem, offers rejected alternative framings with reasons, and defines what "solved" would look like per persona. Use after synthesizing interviews and before scoping, or when someone asks "what problem are we actually solving" or suspects the brief asked for the wrong thing.

skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:prototype-brief
skills.description: Ranks a v1's assumptions by risk and testability, picks the single riskiest one a prototype can test, and writes a build-ready prototype brief — one flow, realistic mock data drawn from the interviews, what's real vs faked, success criteria, a user test script and a paste-ready build prompt. Use after scoping and before building, or when someone asks "what should we prototype first".

skills.name: 4a2ac24d-98e7-40bd-ac96-db035d080871:prototype-build-critique
skills.description: Builds the single-flow prototype described in a prototype brief and then critiques the proposal and prototype as a skeptical head of product — is the "why" clear for the customer and the business, does the prototype test the assumption, which sentences sound AI-written, and what to cut. Use when a prototype brief is ready to build, or when someone wants an honest review of a product proposal, MVP or deck before showing it.

items.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee
items.description: Eleven generic workspace skills that set up and maintain a Claude Cowork workspace safely: setup, hygiene audit, memory routing and tiering, project scaffolding, inbox triage, correspondence logging, a critical-thinking sparring partner, session audit, memory consolidation, a check for switched-off skills and an orientation tour. Nothing changes without your approval, anything replaced is backed up first and nothing you wrote is ever deleted. Install, then say 'what does the EASE OS plugin do'
items.author: Karim Mneimneh

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:consolidate-memory
skills.description: Compresses a memory file that has grown past its soft ceiling, merging and summarising older entries WITHOUT losing any information, so the file stays lean. Use when the user says 'consolidate my memory', 'tidy my memory', 'my memory file is too long', 'compress my memory', 'my memory is over the limit' or 'clean up my memory'. Approval-gated: shows a clear before and after and waits for a yes. Archives, never deletes: original older entries are moved to a memory-archive.md in the same folder so nothing is ever lost. Never raises a ceiling.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:correspondence-log
skills.description: Files a written correspondence the user shares (email, Slack, WhatsApp or any external message thread), or a call transcript or meeting notes, into the right project's contact log as one dense, decision-relevant entry. Use when the user pastes a message or thread and says 'log this to [project]', 'save this to [project] logs', 'add this to my [project] contact log', 'debrief this call' or 'log this call to [project]'. Routes the project via the workspace's routing map, matches the log's own density and style, extracts only what helps a future session decide (who said what, what was decided or requested, what is still open, risks or signals), drops pleasantries and admin noise and shows the proposed entry for a go/adjust/trim/expand sign-off before appending. Proposal-only and append-only: never writes until the user approves, never overwrites or reorders entries. Not for routing a remember-this into project state (use memory-router).

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:disabled-skill-check
skills.description: Checks whether a disabled or deleted skill exists for a task before improvising. Triggers when: the current task would clearly benefit from a specialised skill, no enabled skill in the available list matches it and Claude is about to improvise. Reads about-me/disabled-skills.md, scans for a fit and surfaces the match before proceeding.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:ease-setup
skills.description: Safely optimises a Cowork workspace for the EASE OS kit (sets up what is missing and upgrades what is already there) by comparing the kit against what the user already has. Use when the user says 'optimise my workspace', 'optimize my workspace', 'optimise my Cowork', 'upgrade my workspace', 'compare the kit to what I have' or runs this after installing the kit. Always assumes the user already has a system; never resets or wipes anything. Inventories what exists, preserves everything good, proposes only genuine improvements (missing files or missing sections) for the user's approval item by item and never deletes or overwrites anything without an explicit yes and a backup.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:inbox-triage
skills.description: Walks the user's inbox file item by item, classifies each item and routes it to the right home with their sign-off. Use when the user says "add this to my inbox" (to capture one thought) or "triage my inbox", "process the inbox", "clear my inbox", "what's in my inbox", "let's go through the inbox" or "what did I capture this week". Reads `inbox/inbox.md`, classifies items by type, suggests destinations, asks the user to confirm each move (or a whole group they have seen, if they ask to speed up), then writes the item to its destination, copies it word for word into triaged-archive.md and only then removes it from inbox.md.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:memory-router
skills.description: Routes any 'remember this' moment to the correct file layer before writing. Triggers on: 'remember this', 'remember X', 'save this', 'note this for next time', 'keep this', 'I want to remember', 'make a note', 'noting this' and equivalents, and also when the user locks a rule ('from now on', 'never again', 'this is a hard rule', 'make this permanent') even without a memory word. Not for filing a pasted message or email thread into a project's record, which is the correspondence-log skill. Identifies the correct scope (global, workstation, project, voice, identity), resolves which file to write to and enforces the no-duplication principle. Writes to the determined location and confirms in chat. Does not write before routing is resolved and the user has said yes to the exact entry.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:new-project-setup
skills.description: Scaffolds a new project folder pair in the Cowork workspace. Use when the user says 'start a new project for [name]', 'create a new project for [name]', 'start a new project called [X]', 'set up project [Y]', 'I want to track work on [Z]' or describes a new piece of work that doesn't fit any existing project. Creates matching folders in projects/[name]/ and outputs/[name]/, generates a blank CLAUDE.md and memory.md and asks which workstation it belongs to, showing what it will create before creating it. It also adds a row to up to three files the user already has (their root CLAUDE.md routing map, about-me/memory.md and the workstation's memory.md), showing each row and waiting for a yes before writing it. Follows the structure rules in root CLAUDE.md.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:orientation
skills.description: A friendly, read-only tour of the EASE OS kit: what it can do for the user's workspace and how to start. Use when the user says 'what does the EASE OS plugin do', 'what does EASE OS do', 'what does this plugin do', 'what can this kit do', 'what can you do with my workspace', 'what workspace skills do I have', 'how do I use this kit', 'help me get started', 'getting started' or 'orientation'. Lists the kit's skills with their trigger phrases, gives a short quick start and states the safety promise. Read-only: it changes nothing, creates nothing and deletes nothing.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:session-audit
skills.description: The session close. At the end of a work session, lists everything the session left unfinished and gives each item an outcome, re-checks what the session said was done, then catches the corrections, stated preferences and locked decisions the user made in THIS conversation and proposes saving each one to the right file so the system learns. Use when the user says 'audit this session', 'session audit', 'what did we learn', 'save what we covered', 'end of session check', 'anything to remember from this session', 'debrief this session', 'let's debrief' (with no call notes or thread pasted) or any equivalent. Also offered proactively at the end of a substantial session. Nothing is written until the user has seen it and said yes: memory entries are only ever appended as dated lines, and finishing an unfinished item changes a file only after the user approves the exact change, with a dated backup first if anything is replaced. Never sends or posts anything; never deletes or reorders anything.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:sparring-partner
skills.description: The critical-thinking overlay. Pressure-tests any task, decision, plan, draft or message for blind spots, backfire risk, weak assumptions and higher-leverage alternatives, and judges whether the path reaches the intended outcome. Three gears: a passive high-bar Watch that flags material risk unprompted (kept on by a line ease-setup adds to the workspace); an on-demand 360 Spar on triggers like 'spar with me', 'poke holes', 'red-team this', 'stress-test this', 'what am I missing', 'challenge this', 'play devil's advocate', 'is this the best approach', 'what could backfire'; and a session-end Sweep that runs before the session close. Advisory, never blocking. Defers editorial draft gates and any results-over-time review to the workspace's own domain skills when they exist. Not for making the decision, blocking a ship or manufacturing objections when the work is already strong.

skills.name: cbb09e98-9337-4ea7-ad1a-afb90224c3ee:workspace-hygiene
skills.description: Runs a systems-architect hygiene audit of the user's full Cowork workspace. Use when the user says 'audit my workspace', 'hygiene check', 'clean up my files', 'workspace audit', 'system architect review', 'find redundancies' or wants a structural review of files, memory, routing, dashboards or state files and scheduled tasks. Also reads what scheduled-task instructions say and reports any that have gone stale, without changing them. Not for first-time or repeat setup, which belongs to the ease-setup skill: that one adds what is missing, this one audits what is already there. Produces a severity-ranked report at outputs/system-audits/hygiene-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md, asks about each high and medium finding and proposes low-risk fixes for approval. Also restores a file from its backup or from `_archive/` on 'restore [file] from its backup' or 'move [file] back from the archive'. Different from session-audit (which is end-of-session).

skills.name: d66801a3-e95e-49d4-a427-758679b0b4e4:day-one-setup
skills.description: The guided on-ramp that takes a complete beginner from just-installed Claude Cowork to a safe, working setup, one approved step at a time. Use when the user says 'help me set up Cowork safely', 'EASE Day One', 'start EASE Day One', 'help me get set up on Cowork', 'walk me through setting up Cowork', 'I just installed Cowork, what now' or is a beginner starting from zero. It checks what already exists and continues where they left off; it never assumes a blank slate, never resets anything and never replaces a file without a backup and a yes. It routes install and connecting tools through Cowork's own onboarding rather than repeating those steps, then adds one tightly scoped folder, a minimal workspace and safe defaults (manual approvals, draft-not-send, nothing risky scheduled). First of four Day One skills; it hands on to the first-win skill. It does not build the full workspace system; that is the EASE OS plugin.

skills.name: d66801a3-e95e-49d4-a427-758679b0b4e4:first-win

It briefly asks what the user does over and over in their actual work, takes that single most-repeated task (never a demo or a toy example), gathers the real input and produces the output as a reviewable draft in the working folder or as a Gmail draft. It teaches the approval habit: it shows each step and waits for a yes, and never sends or posts on the user's behalf. Second of four Day One skills. It logs the win to the progress file with the user's approval, then points to the health-check skill ('check my Cowork setup'). If setup is not finished, it routes back to 'help me set up Cowork safely' first. It does not send, publish or schedule, and it does not build the full workspace system, which is the EASE OS plugin.

skills.name: d66801a3-e95e-49d4-a427-758679b0b4e4:graduate
skills.description: The hand-off from EASE Day One to the EASE OS plugin, and the last of the four Day One skills. Use when the user says 'am I ready for EASE OS', 'is my setup ready for EASE OS', 'take me to EASE OS' or has finished setup, logged a first win and passed the health check. It reads the progress file. If the graduation flag is set, it congratulates the user, explains in plain language what EASE OS adds on top of the safe setup they now have, points them to where to get it, walks the same install flow they already know and maps what carries over: their folder, files, connected tools and safety habits all stay, and EASE OS enhances rather than resets. If the flag is not set, it gently explains what is still missing and points to the right next step by its phrase. Read-only and honest: it changes nothing, sets no flag, never overstates EASE OS and recommends rather than requires.

skills.name: d66801a3-e95e-49d4-a427-758679b0b4e4:health-check
skills.description: A re-runnable safety check for an EASE Day One setup, and the gate to graduating into EASE OS. It reads the setup against a short checklist grounded in how Cowork works: one tightly scoped working folder, each connected tool passing a read test, work kept as drafts only, no scheduled task that sends or is hard to undo, a small plugin set and every skill triggering from plain language. If setup has not been done, it routes back to 'help me set up Cowork safely'. It reports and never fixes on its own; the full workspace audit is the EASE OS plugin.

items.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968
items.description: Ten jurisdiction-neutral skills for checking legal AI output before it goes out. Fluency tells you nothing about whether the authority a model cites exists. Each skill either makes one step checkable or attacks the result. citation-extraction-en pulls every citation out of an English text: ECLI (CJEU and national), CELEX and Official Journal references, Regulation and Directive numbers, case names, Article and section references. It then normalises them, drops duplicates, and traces short forms
items.author: Wieslaw Mazur / MateMatic Solutions

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:adversarial-legal-review-en
skills.description: A red team for a high-stakes deliverable - takes a finished, high-stakes document (a legal opinion, a DD/M&A memo, a court/board submission, a recommendation) and runs an adversarial debate: a builder constructs the strongest version of the thesis, an attacker tears it apart with counter-arguments and contrary authority, a synthesizer reconciles, a verifier does a final check. Goal: find the weakness BEFORE your opponent, the court, or the client does. Cost-gated - for high-stakes work only, not every query (token-expensive). Use when: "attack this opinion", "red team", "devil's advocate for this document", "find the weaknesses", "stress-test the argument", "what will the other side say", "pre-mortem", "defend this thesis", "adversarial review", verifying a high-stakes deliverable before it goes out. English counterpart of adversarial-legal-review-pl (this version drops the Polish case-law layer and is jurisdiction-agnostic).

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:citation-extraction-en
skills.description: Extracts the legal citations from an English-language text by pattern and rule, with no LLM in the extraction step, so the same text yields the same list every run - ECLI (CJEU and national), EU act identifiers (CELEX, Official Journal references, Regulation and Directive numbers), case names, and cited provisions (Article/section). It then normalises, deduplicates and resolves short references (ibid., id., supra, op. cit., the above-cited judgment) to their antecedent. The front end to verification: collect what is cited, then check it. Unusual or malformed citation formats can still be missed, so treat the output as a working list rather than a guarantee. Jurisdiction-neutral, EU-aware. Use when: "list every citation in this text", "what authorities are cited", "extract the provisions", "pull the case references", "what is cited here" - before verification or before sending.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:clause-checklist-en
skills.description: A clause checklist for a single contract - walks the contract against 41 clause categories (the CUAD taxonomy), assesses which of them this deal needs, and marks each applicable one present / absent / risky, so the clause that should be there but is missing does not slip through. Extractive (quotes the contract, does not paraphrase). Common-law native, jurisdiction-neutral framing. Different from a bulk audit - this goes deep on one contract and asks "what is missing and what bites here". Pairs with adversarial-legal-review-en and reviewer-en. Use when: "check the clauses in this contract", "what is missing from this agreement", "clause spotting", "contract checklist", "review a single contract", "which clauses are risky" - before signing, in negotiation, or in DD of one contract.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:deliverable-fidelity-en
skills.description: Checks whether the final document still carries what the analysis actually found. Takes the list of findings with their severities and the finished deliverable, runs a mechanical coverage check with a bundled zero-dependency script, then an LLM spot-check on the RED findings for tone-downgrading, and returns a deterministic verdict PASS / CONDITIONAL_PASS / FAIL from published weights and thresholds. An omitted RED finding blocks. The third axis of verification, next to citation checking (are the sources real) and adversarial review (does the thesis hold): this one asks whether the summary is faithful to the analysis. Jurisdiction-neutral. Use when: "does the summary cover everything", "did anything drop out of the executive summary", "fidelity check", "is the deliverable faithful", "check the memo against the findings" - before sending any document that summarises a longer analysis.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:intake-sufficiency-en
skills.description: Scores whether an instruction or brief is complete enough to start work on. Before any legal analysis begins, checks that the purpose, scope, parties, facts, constraints and success criteria are actually present; lists the gaps and ambiguities; turns each gap into a question ready to send to the client; and drafts the skeleton of a matter card. Separates the client's legal assertions from facts and marks them for verification. The mirror of legal-request-router-en: the router decides what control the OUTPUT needs, this decides whether the INPUT is enough to begin. Jurisdiction-neutral. Use when: "do I have enough to start", "score this brief", "what is missing from this instruction", "what should I ask the client", "is this instruction complete", "gaps in the brief", "intake" - at the start of a matter, after first contact, after an intake call.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:judicial-first-impression-en
skills.description: Assesses a legal submission or structured argument from the perspective of a judge reading it COLD, under time pressure, with a docket of several hundred cases. Returns a structured seven-part assessment: what the case appears to be about, immediate points of confusion, what feels strong, what feels weak, what is assumed but unproved, a provisional confidence level (low/medium/high), and what would be needed to persuade. The skill does NOT rewrite, does NOT improve and does NOT attack the submission - it tells you how it actually LANDS on an experienced, sceptical reader with no prior context. Works on statements of claim, appeals, skeleton arguments, motions, position statements, pre-action letters and any structured reasoning. Use when: "how will the court read this", "first impression", "is this clear to the judge", "cold reader test", "how does this land", before filing a court submission.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:legal-request-router-en
skills.description: Triage for a legal request. Looks at the question (and optionally the finished deliverable) and decides which verification path to run: plain answer, citation checking, adversarial review, or the full route. Scores complexity and risk and returns a routing decision with its reasoning and an ordered list of skills to run. A layer above the verification layer: it stops routine work from burning tokens on ceremony, and stops high-stakes work from shipping unchecked. Jurisdiction-neutral. Use when: "what should I do with this", "does this need a full review", "which path", "classify this request", "is this high-stakes", "triage", "routing" - at the start of a new legal request, before picking tools.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:legal-syllogism-en
skills.description: Builds the explicit legal syllogism for an issue - lays out the major premise (the rule and its interpretation), the minor premise (the material facts), the application (subsuming facts under each element of the rule), and the conclusion, then flags the weak links: unstated assumptions, contested facts, debatable interpretation. Forces every step to be said out loud and checkable instead of jumping from facts to a holding. Maps to civil-law subsumption and common-law IRAC/CREAC. Jurisdiction-neutral method: it supplies no rule and checks no citation, so the major premise has to come from a source you trust. Use when: "build the syllogism", "lay out the legal reasoning", "apply the rule to the facts", "IRAC this", "where is the gap in the argument", "major and minor premise", "structure the analysis" - when drafting an opinion, brief, or memo.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:opposing-counsel-attack-en
skills.description: Single-pass opposing counsel attack on a legal argument - takes on the role of experienced counsel for the other side who has been handed your submission and told "find every way to beat this". Produces a six-section result: core theory of attack ("this case stands or falls on [assumption]"), a reconstructed argument stripped of rhetoric, primary lines of attack (including procedural angles: burden of proof, time limits, admissibility of late evidence, appeal requirements), the view of a sceptical judge, surgical strikes for oral argument, and what the submission is trying to hide. Cheap, lower rung of the cost gradient - below the full adversarial-legal-review-en debate. Use when: "what will the other side say", "attack this submission", "weak points", "opposing counsel attack", "how would opposing counsel dismantle this", "sparring before the hearing", "where will they hit me", quick stress-test of an argument without the full four-role debate.

skills.name: 6130fc79-8c47-4c93-b9e9-46e4b4aa8968:output-scoring-en
skills.description: Scores the quality of an AI legal output before it goes out, in two layers: objective (mechanically checkable - do the citations exist, are the provisions and dockets real) and subjective (LLM-as-judge on a 1-5 rubric: legal correctness, completeness, clarity, jurisdiction fit, grounding/anti-hallucination). Returns a scorecard and a decision: send / revise / full verification. A layer above the deliverable - it does not write, it scores. Jurisdiction-neutral. Pairs with reviewer-en, adversarial-legal-review-en and legal-syllogism-en. Use when: "score this output", "is this ready to send", "quality of this legal answer", "scorecard for the deliverable", "rubric check" - before sending an opinion, memo, or brief.

agents.description: Checks the session diff against its plan steps — marks each step followed/deviated, emits a finding plus a review hotspot for every deviation. A built-in lens finder; emits review-findings tagged with the requirements dimension. Read-only.

agents.name: risk-classify
agents.description: Tags each changed file with a blast-radius risk class (auth/data/money/migration/concurrency/public-api/none) and flags high-risk files that lack a test or guard. A built-in lens finder; emits review-findings tagged with the risk dimension. Read-only.

agents.name: spec-adherence

agents.name: test-gaps
agents.description: Identifies new or changed code paths in the session diff that lack test coverage and emits a finding per meaningful untested path. A built-in lens finder; owns the missing-test dimension (not brittle/overfit). Emits review-findings tagged with the test dimension. Read-only.

agents.name: verifier
agents.description: Adversarial skeptic for the lens VERIFY stage — takes ONE candidate finding and tries to refute it against the real source, defaulting to refuted for unproven bug/correctness/security/test claims and kept for spec/plan judgment. Owns the verified flip. Read-only.

skills.name: 9936a499-3bd8-42a2-a94f-a9b3339682e4:hygiene-self-monitoring
skills.description: Change-scope discipline for a fix or a feature that touches shared code. A change can keep the request's check green and still reach past the request - another exported function, a helper other callers use, a sibling fixed 'for consistency', a documented default - and the summary reports it as a matter of course ('it uses the same rule now'). This skill has the agent list the public behaviour its change reaches, mark what the request names, and put back or offer to the owner what it does not, closing with a [HYGIENE CHECK]: Request names, Change reaches, Outside, Decision. Triggers - fix this bug, this issue, while I'm in there, for consistency, the same bug is also in, shared helper, refactor, cleanup, tidy up, small fix, minimal change, public API, exported function, breaking change, deprecated, legacy, keep the change small, scope creep, unrelated change.

skills.name: 31004b88-0db0-40d0-9461-db18243894a9:aspiration-self-monitoring
skills.description: Review-before-you-close discipline for a result about to be called good enough. Meets is a claim about that comparison, never an impression; a result still off is reported as a defect, never as met. Triggers - this is done, good enough, looks good now, ya está listo, se ve bien, lo doy por terminado, the first version that meets the letter, closing without reviewing the result, drawn from memory, a stop while a defect is still there, a shortcut.

items.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2
items.description: Partner management for Claude: research, qualify, onboard, co-sell, QBR, strategy, program design and partner comms workflows, eight role agents, the Partner Program Maturity Assessment, partner health, and every PartnerImpact calculator through the hosted connector. Free. By Bart Dirksen.
items.author: Bart Dirksen (PartnerImpact)

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:co-sell-motion
skills.description: This skill should be used when designing or running a co-sell motion, account mapping, joint close plans, rules of engagement, deal registration, or aligning partner and direct sales teams on a deal. Provides embedded co-sell process references.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:cosell-plan
skills.description: Use this skill for any joint deal or co-sell question with a partner: should this co-sell deal be in the forecast, is this joint opportunity real, build a co-sell plan, map accounts with a partner, work a deal together, rules of engagement, deal registration, or why the field is not working a partner. It scores a named deal on the Co-sell Deal Qualifier through the connector and turns the gaps into next steps.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:diagnose
skills.description: Use this skill when partners are not producing and the cause is unclear: why is X not producing, where did this partner stall, we have partners but no pipeline, where is the funnel leaking, partner deals are not closing. It finds which conversion is failing for one partner, one motion or the whole base, and whether the cause is the partner, the program or the incentives.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:onboard
skills.description: Use this skill once a partner has signed: onboard X, a 90-day or 30-60-90 plan, a ramp or enablement plan, certification milestones, is onboarding on track, why a signed partner is not activating or producing. It builds a dated plan with checkable milestones and owners on both sides, sized to the people the user actually has.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-brief
skills.description: Use this skill for a short written profile of one partner or prospect: a one-pager, a partner brief, a summary for a leadership meeting, or a quick profile with a go or no-go. It is built from public evidence plus a few questions.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-comms
skills.description: Use this skill to write any message to or about a partner: a note or email to a partner, a follow-up, the joint value proposition, an executive update on a partnership, and hard messages such as a tier demotion, a missed commitment or an exit.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-economics
skills.description: This skill should be used when working on partner economics, revenue attribution (sourced/influenced/co-sold), rev-share and margin models, partner CAC, MDF ROI, program ROI, a multi-year business case, pipeline targets, KPIs, QBR attainment, referral fees, co-marketing ROI, alliance valuation, build/partner/buy, the most a partner can be paid, portfolio concentration, or revenue at risk. Provides embedded references and calculators for the commercial math of partnerships.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-frameworks
skills.description: This skill should be used when sizing the partner team or funnel, simulating the program, choosing a channel mix, assessing a partner function, scoring a prospective partner, designing tiers or segmentation, or diagnosing why a partner program underperforms. Provides the core embedded frameworks: partner function maturity model, ideal-partner profile, lifecycle bowtie, and tiering & segmentation.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-health-check
skills.description: Use this skill for any question about how one existing partner is doing: how is X doing, is X at risk, should we worry about X, X has gone quiet, their sponsor left, a health read on X. It rates six signals red, amber or green on the connector, applies the rules that decide at-risk, and names the one move to make this week. Works for any partner type, and not knowing is a valid answer to every question.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-maturity-check
skills.description: Use this skill for any question about the state of the user's own partner function or program: how mature are we, assess or audit our partner program, how do we compare with companies our size, what should we fix first, where are the gaps. It runs the PartnerImpact Partner Program Maturity Assessment, quick (twelve questions, about five minutes) or full (forty-eight, one domain at a time), and ends on the binding constraint: the one thing to fix before anything downstream will stick.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-motions
skills.description: This skill should be used when the partner's motion type matters, qualifying, enabling, pricing, or co-selling with a referral partner, reseller, technology/integration partner, marketplace, services SI, or strategic alliance. Provides the per-type deltas: what shifts in qualification, economics, enablement, and co-sell for each.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-numbers
skills.description: Use this skill for every question that needs a partner-related figure, even when the arithmetic looks simple enough to do directly: how much pipeline a revenue target needs and how much of it partners must source, the rev-share, margin or referral fee a partner can be paid, program ROI or payback, MDF split, partner manager capacity, churn or concentration risk, build versus partner versus buy, KPIs. It runs the matching PartnerImpact calculator on the connector instead of working by hand, shows which inputs were the user's and which were defaults, and leads with the decision the number supports.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-os
skills.description: Use this skill when the user wants help with partners but has not said with what: what can you help me with, where do I start, help me with my partners, where does this partner stand, what should I do next with X, what is stalled. It offers the jobs the plugin does in plain words, places a partner on the lifecycle and routes to the right skill instead of doing the work itself.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-research
skills.description: This skill should be used when gathering public evidence on a company ahead of a partnership decision, finding their ecosystem and named partners, establishing their motion type, reading commitment signals, or grading how much a piece of evidence is worth. Provides embedded sourcing and confidence-grading references.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:partner-strategy
skills.description: Use this skill for partner strategy questions: build a partner strategy, where to play with partners, which partner types to prioritise, how to segment partners, build versus partner versus buy for a capability, or the leverage thesis for a partner program.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:program-architecture
skills.description: This skill should be used when designing or refining a partner program, tier structure, benefit stacks, partner incentives, MDF, or the enablement and certification path, including tier economics, quotas, MDF allocation, activation readiness and onboarding tracking. Provides embedded design references for program architecture.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:program-design
skills.description: Use this skill to design or change a partner program: tiers and tier criteria, benefits, incentives, MDF, a certification path, tier economics, or how to tier an existing partner base.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:qbr-prep
skills.description: Use this skill for any partner review or performance question: prepare a QBR or business review, attainment against plan or target, a partner scorecard, where a review conversation should start, renew or prune a partner. Use it whenever the user gives targets and actuals for a partner. It bands attainment on the connector, reads partner health, and ends on at most three asks with owners on both sides.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:qualify
skills.description: Use this skill for any decision about taking on, signing or keeping a specific partner: should we partner with, sign, onboard or resell through X, is X a good fit, qualify or score X, go or no-go on X. Use it even when the user lists the facts and only asks for a verdict. Run it before answering, because it checks five deal-breakers (channel conflict, brand risk, no new reach, no senior owner, economics underwater) ahead of any scoring, then returns go, conditional go, not yet or no-go against the ideal partner profile.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:research
skills.description: Use this skill to find out about a company before a partnership decision: research X, who does X partner with, what is X's ecosystem, look up X, build an evidence log for X. It gathers public evidence and grades each claim A, B or C with its source, without scoring or recommending.

skills.name: 65852db7-26ee-45c0-9df7-067ab4f0a0f2:ideal-partner-profile
skills.description: Use this skill to build or revise the criteria for choosing partners of one kind: create an ideal partner profile, an IPP, a partner scorecard, selection criteria or a scoring model for resellers, referrers, technology partners, marketplaces, service firms or alliances, or decide how to weight what matters in a partner. It builds the profile for one partner motion from a starter, with weights that sum to 100, 1-3-5 anchors in the user's own terms and deal-breakers, and tests it against partners the user already knows. Not for profiling one named company.

agents.name: cosell-lead
agents.description: Playbook for co-sell work with a partner. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: cosell-plan. Triggers: "build a co-sell plan for X", "map accounts with X", "help me work this deal with X", "write rules of engagement", "set up deal registration", "why isn't the field working the partner". Owns the Co-sell stage.

agents.name: partner-communicator
agents.description: Playbook for partner and executive messages. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: partner-comms. Triggers: "draft a note to X", "write the JVP for X", "follow up with X", "write the exit message for X", "exec update on the partnership". Supports every stage; owns the communication layer.

agents.name: partner-diagnostician
agents.description: Playbook for diagnosing a partner function or a stalled partner. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: partner-maturity-check, diagnose. Triggers: "assess our partner function", "how mature is our program", "what should we fix first", "why isn't X producing", "diagnose X", "where are we stuck", "we have partners but no pipeline". Produces a diagnosis and a binding constraint, not a design.

agents.name: partner-enablement-lead
agents.description: Playbook for partner onboarding and activation. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: onboard. Triggers: "onboard X", "build the 90-day plan for X", "what training does X need", "why isn't X activating", "is X's onboarding on track", "design the certification path". Owns the Onboard stage end to end.

agents.name: partner-performance
agents.description: Playbook for partner performance, reviews and economics. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: qbr-prep, partner-health-check, partner-numbers. Triggers: "prep the QBR for X", "how is X performing", "build a scorecard", "is X at risk", "what's the ROI on X", "check the attribution", "should we renew or prune X". Owns the Grow and Renew/Prune stages.

agents.name: partner-qualifier
agents.description: Playbook for qualifying a partner. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: qualify, partner-brief. Triggers: "should we partner with X", "qualify X", "score X", "is X a good fit", "go/no-go on X", "profile X". Owns the Qualify stage of the lifecycle.

agents.name: partner-researcher
agents.description: Use to gather public evidence on a company before a partnership decision, what they do, their motion type, their existing ecosystem and named partners, marketplace and integration listings, ICP overlap signals, and executive commitment signals. Triggers: "research X", "who does X partner with", "what's X's ecosystem", "look up X", "what do we know about X", "build an evidence log for X". Owns the Recruit stage's evidence work. Produces a graded evidence log, never a score.

agents.name: partner-strategist
agents.description: Playbook for partner strategy and program design. For anything that needs the user's answers, run the matching skill in the main conversation instead of delegating: partner-strategy, program-design. Triggers: "build a partner strategy", "design our program", "how should we tier partners", "map our ecosystem", "where are our partner gaps", "should we partner for X" (build/partner/buy). Owns the Recruit and Onboard stages of the lifecycle at the design level.

items.name: f6ae5033-7c31-450c-a3b9-b88d6c27e2e1
items.description: Interactive, self-contained HTML docs for any project: infrastructure topology, AI/LLM workflow diagrams and an evidence-backed user guide, exportable to PDF and Word.
items.author: Bhargava Ganti

skills.name: f6ae5033-7c31-450c-a3b9-b88d6c27e2e1:interactive-docs
skills.description: Generate self-contained, interactive HTML documentation for ANY software project — web app, CLI, mobile app, backend API, data/ML pipeline or library: (1) a DEPLOYMENT / INFRASTRUCTURE doc with a clickable topology, data flow, containers, storage, seeding runbook, security and deploy steps; (2) an AI WORKFLOWS doc with mermaid diagrams of every model call — agent loops, RAG index/query paths, guardrails — plus prompt inventory, context & data path, failure modes and cost; and (3) an interactive USER GUIDE / usage walkthrough with a flow tree, real evidence (screenshots, terminal transcripts or request/response pairs) and per-step "who does what". Use when the user asks to build/produce an interactive usage guide, product tutorial, onboarding walkthrough, "how the app works" doc, an architecture or infrastructure diagram, an AI/LLM/RAG/agent pipeline diagram, a deployment/ops doc, or a client-facing explainer of a running system.

items.name: 077a09f6-5297-466e-950d-02c2b9ac4169
items.description: Paints Markdown onto Claude Code's prompt box as you type: fenced code becomes a syntax-highlighted card (even before you close the fence), and inline code, bold, italic, lists, task lists, quotes, tables, links and headings are styled. Paint only, your text is never changed.
items.author: nogu66

items.name: d7058bee-dbd3-4f23-bc2e-69f260a9cd97
items.description: Search, compare and view current IT job offers published on theprotocol.it in Poland.
items.author: theprotocol.it

skills.name: d7058bee-dbd3-4f23-bc2e-69f260a9cd97:theprotocol-job-search
skills.description: Searches and displays IT job offers from theprotocol.it using the the:protocol MCP server (search_job_offers, get_job_offer_details, get_dictionary_elements). Use this skill whenever the user wants to find, browse or look up job offers, vacancies or IT roles — e.g. "znajdź oferty dla senior Java developera w Krakowie", "szukam pracy zdalnej z Pythonem", "pokaż szczegóły tej oferty", "jakie są oferty w firmie X", "find remote React jobs over 20k" — even if theprotocol.it is not mentioned by name, and whenever the user asks about requirements, salary or work mode of a specific offer from the results. Do not use it for non-IT jobs, writing CVs or cover letters, or general career advice without a request for offers.

items.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7
items.description: Helps a small team decide which marketing ideas deserve money, and whether a test worked. Describe your product and it suggests one main bet and two cheap tests, dropping ideas that break disclosure or platform rules; paste your own list and it ranks it. For one idea, such as a sponsorship or a booth, it works out the most you can pay per customer and per click and whether a quoted price fits. It sets pass and stop lines before a test and reads the results afterwards, showing each rate with its
items.author: Sergey Skripko

skills.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7:idea-payback-check
skills.description: Says whether one named marketing idea is worth its cost before money is spent: a sponsorship, a booth, a launch-platform day, a lifetime-deal listing, a partner listing or a referral reward. Gives a verdict (Go, Test small first or Not now), the numbers it rests on, the most the user can afford to pay, and the cheapest way to find out. Use when the user names one idea and asks should we, is it worth it, what can we afford or will it pay back. Not for choosing among several ideas, reading results of a test already run, or judging an ad account's performance.

skills.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7:idea-ranking
skills.description: Ranks the user's own list of marketing or acquisition ideas (channels, tactics, offers) and names the ones to test first, with the reason and what would lift each lower idea. Reads vague ideas in their most plausible form, merges duplicates, sets aside product features, pricing changes and content topics, and drops ideas that break disclosure or platform rules or fail on a cost the user gave. Use when the user pastes several marketing ideas and asks which to test first or how to rank them. Not for lists of article or content topics, and not for coming up with ideas from scratch.

skills.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7:idea-readout
skills.description: Reads counts from marketing channel tests the user already ran (sent, visits, replies, signups, trials, paying customers, spend) and gives each channel one decision, scale, run another bounded round, stop or inconclusive, with the reason. Applies any pass and stop lines set before the test, compares cost per customer with what a customer may cost, and checks for data problems and coincidences such as a price change. Use when the user pastes channel test results and asks which channels to keep, scale or stop. Not for comparing ad versions or page variants, finding where a site funnel loses people, results by lead magnet, recurring reports from connected tools, or one ad account on its own.

skills.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7:idea-shortlist
skills.description: Suggests which marketing or customer-acquisition ideas to test first for a product the user describes, fitted to its buyer, price, budget and what the team already has. Returns one main bet, at most two cheap tests and a concrete first step; drops ideas that break disclosure or platform rules or cost more than a customer is worth on the user's own figures. Use when the user describes a product, even in one line, and asks what marketing to try, for growth ideas or how to get customers. Not for ranking the user's own list, checking one named idea, getting more signups from a page that already has visitors, campaign plans or content calendars, or writing ad copy.

skills.name: 6ad962f1-50d2-4114-8706-d6584131b1e7:idea-test-card
skills.description: Sets up a test for one to three marketing ideas or channels already chosen, before launch: what counts as working, pass and stop lines tied to what a customer may cost or to the user's goal, whether the expected volume can show a result, cash and hours caps, and when to read the result. Use when the user has picked ideas or channels and asks how to test them, how to set up a growth experiment, what counts as working, or for pass and stop lines. Not for A/B tests of two page versions.

items.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4
items.description: Pick a lead magnet for what you sell and decide whether to gate it; draft it from your own material with no invented figures; check an opt-in page, form, thank-you page and confirmation email against dated US, EU and UK consent and sender rules; plan what each sign-up may receive given the consent it gave; and compare sign-up and sales-call rates by magnet, with honest ranges for small numbers. Checks, not legal advice.
items.author: Sergey Skripko

skills.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4:magnet-build
skills.description: Writes a lead magnet the user has already chosen (checklist, template, scorecard, calculator spec, worksheet, workshop plan, short guide) from the team's own notes, process, sheet or formula, plus download-page copy. Keeps every figure to the user's material. Use when the user asks to write, outline or spec a lead magnet or free download from their material. Not for choosing which magnet to make, visual design or calculator code.

skills.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4:magnet-followup
skills.description: Says who may be emailed after a lead magnet download, and with what, from the consent each person gave under US, EU and UK rules, and where a person takes over. Can audit a pasted sign-up export for consent record problems without printing any email. Use when the user asks whether or what they may email people who downloaded something, what consent proof to keep, or brings a sign-up export to check. Writes no email copy.

skills.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4:magnet-plan
skills.description: Picks a lead magnet for what the company sells and decides whether to gate it, with the form fields and consent box wording for US, EU and UK visitors. Use when the user asks what to give away for their product, which lead magnet to create, whether to gate an ebook, report or tool, or which fields and consent wording a new sign-up form needs. Not for a content plan, topic cluster or content calendar.

skills.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4:magnet-readout
skills.description: Compares the user's own lead magnets from their numbers or export (visits, sign-ups, sales calls or deals, spend per magnet and traffic source) and says which one to keep. Uses no industry rates. Use when the user gives such numbers or asks which of their lead magnets works or brings sales calls. Not for A/B test design, sample sizes, or channel results not split by magnet.

skills.name: 71a61354-7ffe-48d2-8f0a-d9343e6316e4:optin-check
skills.description: Checks a lead magnet's opt-in page, sign-up form, thank-you page or confirmation email for US, EU and UK consent, honest claims and field use, and rewrites only the lines that are wrong. Use when the user pastes or links their own opt-in or download page, form or confirmation email and asks whether it is right, legal or GDPR compliant. Not for usability reviews, page layout, or demo and checkout forms.

items.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924
items.description: Get sellers ready and keep them sharp. Score a call you want coached against a behaviour rubric with a quoted line behind every score and recomputable talk and question counts; certify reps with a knowledge check keyed to your own material and a role-play buyer who keeps facts back until asked; plan a demo where every scene answers a pain the buyer stated; find which recurring buyer questions your sellers answer without proof, not at all, or differently; and plan a rep's path to selling alone
items.author: Sergey Skripko

skills.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924:call-coaching
skills.description: Coaches one seller from one to five call transcripts or detailed call notes. Scores 11 discovery rows (CS-01 to CS-12, maximum 11 × 2 = 22; CS-11 is a claims list) or 8 demo rows (CS-D01 to CS-D08, maximum 16) on a 0/1/2 behaviour scale, each score backed by a verbatim quote with turn or timestamp, or marked "not observed"; computes seller word share, open and closed questions across call thirds, longest turn and a next-step test with the counting rules printed; lists the numbers, comparisons and customer references the seller stated; gives two strengths, at most two rewrites and one drill. Use when the user asks to coach, score or review a sales call, or what the seller should have done differently. Also use when the user asks to rank, rate or compare sellers or candidates, or to decide firing, bonus, promotion or hiring from call scores or quiz results, so the request is declined and a coaching plan offered. Not for writing up what happened on the call.

skills.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924:demo-runbook
skills.description: Plans a sales demo from discovery notes, or checks an existing demo script. Builds a pain ledger from what the buyer said, a scene table that gives each stated pain one scene with a proof slot and minutes, an outcome-first opening, open check-ins before and after each scene, a don't-show list of capabilities no pain asks for, and the discovery gaps to ask about first; then runs PASS or FIX checks on pain coverage, scene count, time against the slot, closed check-ins, proof and a closing next-step line. Use when the user asks to plan, outline or structure a product demo or its run of show, or to check a demo script, for a buyer whose needs are known. Not for booking the meeting or a general briefing before a meeting.

skills.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924:question-bank
skills.description: Checks what sellers answer when buyers ask the same question across three or more sales conversations that include seller turns (transcripts, email threads, chat logs). Groups buyer questions with a printed merge rule, counts conversations per question with a Wilson 95% interval, quotes each distinct seller answer, and marks it answered with proof, answered without proof, no answer, or contradictory between sellers; ranks the answer gaps, proposes one answer per gap only from the user's material, and diffs against a previous bank. Use when the user asks where sellers' answers are missing, unproven or inconsistent, or wants one agreed answer per recurring buyer question, or an existing bank updated. Not for collecting buyer quotes on a topic or comparing won and lost deals.

skills.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924:ramp-plan
skills.description: Plans how a seller in a sales role (SDR, AE, AM, sales engineer, or the first seller after a founder) becomes ready to run calls and deals alone. Derives the plan length from the user's median sales cycle (the solo phase lasts at least one cycle), sets certification gates that reuse the plugin's quoted call rubric and knowledge checks, computes coach hours per week from a printed hour model against the hours the coach has, flags overload weeks, maps each milestone to a Kirkpatrick evaluation level, and lists missing practice material. Use when the user asks how long until a seller can sell alone, for a sales ramp, or for a certification path for a sales role, or whether the coaching hours cover it. Not for first-day checklists, day-count goal plans for new employees, general new-employee goals or sales targets.

skills.name: f8cb9758-af5d-482d-bd56-49ba50d33924:rep-certification
skills.description: Certifies sellers on the user's own material and rehearses calls. Numbers the source into lines S1, S2 and writes a 10 to 20 item knowledge check whose answer key cites those lines, listing questions the source cannot answer as source gaps instead of guessing; builds a role-play buyer with four to six hidden facts that are revealed only when the rep asks the question that earns them; can play that fictional buyer live, then scores the role-play with the plugin's quoted 0/1/2 rubric (11 discovery rows, maximum 22) and lists facts found and missed; applies a stated pass rule and a retest schedule. Use when the user asks to quiz, test or certify sellers, to rehearse or role-play a sales conversation, to "play the buyer", or "drill me". Not for preparing a specific upcoming meeting, and not for ranking people from results.

items.name: 414adef7-cca1-42ff-8eb6-52b2b151888d
items.description: Build and manage repository-backed web apps with Samebase, GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare.
items.author: Samebase

skills.name: 414adef7-cca1-42ff-8eb6-52b2b151888d:samebase
skills.description: Use Samebase to create and manage web apps in Samebase repositories: a GitHub repository with optional Convex projects and Cloudflare Workers. Use when the user asks to list, create, connect, configure, repair, open, publish, or operate a Samebase repository or app, review or apply changes from the starter changelog, or submit feedback about Samebase.

items.name: 41f4eed9-a8ad-4572-9d8d-95d4aeb26ed1
items.description: Build durable workflows and inspect Inngest Cloud apps, functions, events, runs, and traces through OAuth MCP.
items.author: Inngest, Inc.

skills.name: 41f4eed9-a8ad-4572-9d8d-95d4aeb26ed1:inngest-agents
skills.description: Use when building durable AI agents or agentic workflows with Inngest and AgentKit, including model calls, tool calls, multi-agent networks, human approval, realtime progress, provider rate limits, and crash-safe execution. Covers AgentKit, `step.ai`, `step.run`, `step.waitForEvent`, native realtime, and when to use lower-level Inngest primitives instead of an in-memory agent loop.

Remove signs of AI-generated writing from text. Use when editing or reviewing

comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, passive
voice, negative parallelisms, filler phrases, flat rhythm and noun-heavy syntax.
Minimal edits: it changes wording, not content - a post-edit check (stdlib
script) guards dates, amounts, legal references, case numbers, quotations, the
force of obligations, certainty and legal terms. Contracts and pleadings get a
legal-register mode.

artykuly, aktualnosci, posty LinkedIn, maile, scenariusze, copy stron, dokumentacja.
Wykrywa: inflacje znaczeniowa, slop-slownictwo PL, imieslowy pozornej glebi,
vague attributions, naduzycie em-dash, regule trojki, hedging, artefakty czatbota,
kalki anglicyzmow, pisownie sprzed reformy RJP 2026, monotonny rytm i skladnie
rzeczownikowa. Minimalna ingerencja: zmienia slowa, nie tresc - bramka po
przepisaniu (skrypt stdlib) pilnuje dat, kwot, przepisow, sygnatur, cytatow, sily
normy, pewnosci i terminow prawnych. Umowy i pisma: tryb rejestru prawniczego.

skills.name: de0fd670-14bf-4603-b92d-96a31bf2361a:humanizer-pt

Adaptação brasileira de blader/humanizer (MIT), irmã de humanizer-pl e humanizer-en.
Use para editar conteúdo em português: páginas de site, artigos,
posts, e-mails, documentação, llms.txt. Detecta: inflação de importância, vocabulário-slop
em português, gerundismo, "mesmo" pronominal, fuga da cópula, atribuição vaga,
travessão, regra de três, hedging, artefatos de chatbot, decalques do inglês,

datas, valores, dispositivos legais, números de processo, citações, a força da
norma, a certeza e os termos jurídicos. Contratos e peças: modo registro jurídico.

items.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10
items.description: A coordinated engineering team of named AI specialists that remembers your project between sessions. Call yui to route work, or call any specialist directly: Go (jaan, siim, mart), Angular (liis, kadi, tiiu), iOS (ren, shu, ryo), Python (eero, anu, ivo), React (noa, rui, aki), SQL (saku), NoSQL (remo), architecture for any stack (kai), process management (enn), and DevOps/infra (sora). Each ships as both a skill and a subagent. Bundled hooks capture finished work when a session ends and say at
items.author: Anna Veretennykova

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:aki
skills.description: Reviews React and TypeScript code for correctness, performance, accessibility, and consistency before it ships. Read-only, never edits; reports findings ranked by severity. Send writing to noa, a bug to rui.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:anu
skills.description: Finds and fixes a specific Python bug: a traceback, a failing test, wrong output, an exception. Reproduces it first and changes only what is broken. Send new Python to eero, a review to ivo.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:eero
skills.description: Writes and edits Python code from a spec: features, modules, functionality. Send a specific bug to anu, a review to ivo.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:enn
skills.description: Starts, stops, and inspects running processes and dev servers: launching a Go binary or a dev server, killing a process by port or name, checking what holds a port. It manages processes and does not edit code.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:ivo
skills.description: Reviews Python code for quality, correctness, security, and style before it ships. Read-only, never edits. Send writing to eero, a bug to anu.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:jaan
skills.description: Writes and edits Go code from a spec: features, endpoints, new packages, functionality. Send a specific bug to siim, a review to mart, a design to kai.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:kadi
skills.description: Finds and fixes a specific Angular or TypeScript bug: a broken component, a wrong render, a failing API call, a compile error. Finds the root cause first and changes only what is broken. Send new features to liis, a review to tiiu.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:kai
skills.description: Designs and specs before any code is written, in any stack: a new system, interfaces and module boundaries, a technical spec. Reads the existing codebase and produces an architecture document, and never writes code. Hands the spec to the stack's implementer (jaan for Go, noa for React, eero for Python, and so on).

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:liis
skills.description: Writes and edits Angular and TypeScript features from a spec: components, routes, services, templates, signals. Send a specific bug to kadi, a review to tiiu.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:mart
skills.description: Reviews Go code for quality, security, and architecture before it merges. Read-only, never edits; reports findings ranked by severity. Good after jaan or siim, or on any Go about to ship. Send writing to jaan, a bug to siim.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:noa
skills.description: Writes and edits React and TypeScript from a spec: components, hooks, state, features. Send a specific bug to rui, a review to aki.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:remo
skills.description: Models document and key-value data and its access patterns, for stores like MongoDB, DynamoDB, and Redis. Send relational schema and SQL to saku.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:ren
skills.description: Writes and edits Swift and iOS features with SwiftUI from a spec: screens, views, data models, following Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Send a specific bug to shu, a review to ryo.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:rui
skills.description: Finds and fixes a specific React bug: a render error, broken state, a stale closure, a bad effect, wrong UI behavior. Reproduces it first and changes only what is broken. Send new React to noa, a review to aki.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:ryo
skills.description: Reviews Swift and iOS code for quality, memory safety, and Human Interface Guidelines compliance before an App Store submission. Read-only, never edits. Good after ren or shu. Send writing to ren, a bug to shu.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:saku
skills.description: Handles relational database work: designing schema, writing and tuning SQL, and writing safe migrations, always from the current schema. Send document and key-value work to remo.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:shu
skills.description: Finds and fixes a specific Swift or iOS bug: a crash, wrong behavior, a rendering problem. Finds the root cause first and changes only what is broken. Send new features to ren, a review to ryo.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:siim
skills.description: Finds and fixes a specific Go bug: an error, a panic, a test failure, wrong behavior. Finds the root cause first and changes only the broken path. Send new features to jaan, a review to mart.

skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:sora
skills.description: Writes and maintains Dockerfiles, CI/CD pipelines (for example GitHub Actions), and infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation): builds, deploys, and environment config, across any stack. skills.name: 8d0c1774-f932-44e2-8b61-1f09a6426b10:untrust
skills.description: Stop applying this project's kumi rules file.
